mapping.heading: ## On GitHub Copilot CLI
lines: JBIT was written for Claude Code; this copy is generated for GitHub Copilot CLI. Where the text or the hook's messages use Claude's names, read them this way:

- **Agents.** An Agent call is Copilot's `task` tool: `agent_type` (`general-purpose` for a builder or verifier, `research` for research, `code-review` or `security-review` for a review), `name`, `description`, `prompt`, and `mode` `"sync"` or `"background"` (poll a background agent with `read_agent`). Pass `model` and `reasoning_effort` only as the plan's Models line sets them; a model id the account doesn't offer fails and is retried without it.

- **No worktree isolation.** `task` has no `isolation: "worktree"`. Build leaves one at a time in the main tree, or in parallel only when each builder owns files no other touches; there is no branch to merge back.

- **Skills.** A `jbit:<name>` skill is the `skill` tool with `{"skill": "<name>"}`, typed by the user as `/jbit:<name>`. A typed `/plan`, `/review` or `/autopilot` is Copilot's own command, not JBIT's.
- **Questions.** Where a skill says to ask the user (AskUserQuestion on Claude Code), ask in the chat and wait for the reply.

- **Reviews.** `/code-review` and `/security-review` are Claude Code commands. Here, run a `task` agent with `agent_type: "code-review"` (seen working), or a fresh `general-purpose` agent briefed with the same lenses. `security-review` is listed in the `task` tool's agent types but wasn't seen called; if it fails, brief a fresh `general-purpose` agent with the security lens.
- **Instructions.** Copilot reads `CLAUDE.md` too; also read `AGENTS.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` when they exist.

- **Script paths.** `<verify skill folder>` in a skill's command is a placeholder: put in the folder holding the verify skill's `SKILL.md` in the installed JBIT plugin, never a path inside the project (a project's own `scripts/capture.mjs` isn't JBIT's). Run the script by that full path from the project, so its other paths (`--out docs/evidence/…`) stay relative to the project.

gaps.why: Each hook event is a fresh process, so nothing counts repeated turn ends; Copilot's cap of 8 agentStop blocks per prompt bounds the loop instead.

gaps.what: Lean's count of agents already running
gaps.why: The Claude hook keeps it in memory across events; a command hook has no running process to keep it in.
Same reason: no in-memory agent list between events.

gaps.what: The reopen check after a commit
gaps.why: It runs before the commit lands, since there's no in-memory state carried to the next event.
Covered on their documented shape with fixture tests only: no model this account offers writes through them, so no live run proved them. `bash` and `apply_patch` are proven.
agentStop gets 8 blocks per prompt, so an unattended run stops quietly at its 9th turn end; use Copilot's --autopilot or prompt again.
They are Copilot's own commands; type `/jbit:plan`, `/jbit:review`, `/jbit:autopilot`.
The hook runs the Claude hook's TypeScript through Node's type stripping; an older Node can't load it, so guarded tool calls are refused.
They are Claude Code built-ins; on Copilot the review runs as a `task` agent (`code-review`, `security-review`) or a fresh agent with the same lenses.
Copilot's `task` has none, so parallel builders must own separate files or run one at a time.

gaps.what: Compacting the context before autopilot carries on
gaps.why: Copilot gives a command hook no context gauge and no compact call (the shim reports 0% and skips compaction); Copilot manages its own context.

gaps.what: The stage hold and the secret guard inside a `task` subagent
gaps.why: Only the commit gate was proven inside a subagent (stage 4, run 12); in the runs meant to test the hold and the secret guard there, the model declined to delegate, so those two are unproven in a subagent.

gaps.what: A hook that hangs or prints junk
gaps.why: Copilot refuses a call when a preToolUse hook exits non-zero, but lets the call run when the hook prints something other than JSON or outlasts its 30-second timeout (proven at stage 4 on a scratch copy). The shipped hook prints only JSON and refuses by its own 25-second watchdog, so this bites only if the hook's event loop blocks.
They are the Claude hook's words and name Claude tools (Agent, Edit, Write); each skill's mapping section translates them.

Skills name it as `<verify skill folder>/scripts/capture.mjs`, a placeholder the model fills with the installed plugin's verify skill folder, where Claude Code puts in the exact path itself. Copilot's docs say a skill's folder is open to the model, but no live run has yet shown that the model sees its path.
